All of the following are example of sensory, or neural, adaptation EXCEPT:
Option A: After putting on a shirt, you eventually no longer feel the sensation of the fabric on your back.
Option B: After first walking into a crowded room, you no longer are distracted by the buzz of conversation around you.
Option C: After first walking outside on a sunny day, you no longer are blinded by the initial brightness of the light.
Option D: After first walking into an anatomy lab, you no longer notice the smell of formaldehyde.
